blocks.text: Queen Elizabeth I granted the East India Company a charter (license) on December 31, 1600.
The charter gave the company the exclusive right to trade with the East including India.
THE COMPANY RULE (1773-1858)
Regulating Act 1773:
1. Governor of Bengal was converted to Governor General of Bengal.
2. 1st Governor General of Bengal: Warren Hastings 3. Creation of executive council of 4 members to assist Governor General.
4. Bombay and Madras Presidencies made subordinate to Bengal.
5. Establishment of Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774), (1 Chief Justice + 3 other judges).
6. It prohibited the company servants from taking any Bribe or Presents from Indians.
7. Court of Directors (to manage commercial functions) - will report on its Revenue, Civil and Military affairs.
Warren Hastings: The last Governor of Bengal + 1st Gov. General of Bengal.
Elijah Impey: 1st Chief Justice of SC (Calcutta) pre-independence.
Justice Harilal Kania: 1st Chief Justice of India post independence.
Amending Act, 1781:
1. It was passed to rectify the defects of regulating act 1773, it is also known as the Act of Settlement.
2. Exempted the Governor-General and Council from the jurisdiction of Supreme Court.
Pitt's India Act, 1784 (named after William Pitt the Younger)
1. It created Board of Control to manage administrative affairs ie. dual control system started from here.
2. It was called as "Half Loaf System" as it sought to mediate between parliament and the company directors.

3. For the first time company territories in India was called as british possessions in India. lhe Dual Control (Half Loaf System) = Commercial functions Administrative to be managed by functions to be managed Court of Directors by Board of Control Charter Act of 1793 1. It extended the trade monopoly of the company in India for another period of 20 years.
2. Commander-in-chief was not to be a member of the Gov-General council, unless he was so appointed.
3. Members of the Board of Control and staff were to be paid out of the Indian Revenue.
Charter Act of 1813

1. It formally ended the East India Company's trade monopoly over the Indian market, reflecting the shift in British economic policy towards free trade and continued the monopoly of the Company over trade in tea and trade with China.
2. It asserted the Sovereignty of the British crown over the company's territories in India.
3. It allowed Christian Missionaries to come to India: To promote Christianity.
4. Rs. 1 Lakh was allotted to be spent on Indian Education.
5. It authorised the local governments in India to impose taxes on persons and punish the persons for not doing so.
1st Christian Missionary Organisation, Serampore Mission was founded by: William Carey (in 1800).
1st Christian Missionary in India: Thomas Apostle.
Charter Act of 1833 (Also known as "Saint Helena Act)
1. Governor-General of Bengal converted to Governor General of India. (1st: Lord William Bentinck)
2. Deprived the Governor of Bombay and Madras of their legislative powers.
3. It ended activities of EIC as a commercial body, became purely administrative body (lost monopoly trade with China).
4. It provided for the establishment of Law Commission of India to consolidate and codify Indian laws.
5. It attempted to introduce a system of open competition for selection of Civil Servants.
6. A law member to be in Govenor's Executive Council.
(Thomas Babington Macaulay was appointed as its 1st Law member).
7. It completely abolished all commercial activities of the East India Company and transformed it into a purely administrative body responsible for the governance of British territories in India.
Charter Act of 1853
1. Separated legislative and administrative functions of the Governor General's Council.
2. Under it, there was an addition of 6 new members to Council as Legislative Councillors.
3. It introduced Open Competition for Civil Services.
4. It extended the Company rule in Indian Territory, but period was not specified.
5. Introduced, Local Representation in the Indian Legislative Council.
l 6. of the 6 Legislative Members of the Governor-General's council 4 members were appointed by the local govern- ment of Madras, Bombay, Bengal and Agra.
The Crown Rule (1858-1947)
Government of India Act, 1858 (Also known as "Queen's Proclamation")
1. Abolished the East India Company, and transferred the powers of Government, territories and revenues to the British Crown.
2. It changed the designation of Governor General of India to that of Viceroy of India; Lord Canning became the 1st Viceroy of India.
3. It ended the system of Dual Government by abolishing the Board of Control and Court of Directors.
4. It created a new office of Secretary of State for India assisted by a 15-member council with complete authority and control over Indian administration.
Peel Commission 1858 (after 1857 Revolt)
It suggested reforms and the British Government accepted the recommendations and redesigned the Indian military.
Indian Council Act, 1861
1. Associated Indians with law making process. In 1862, Viceroy Lord Canning nominated three Indians to the legislative council. (Raja of Benaras, Maharaja of Patiala and Sir Dinkar Rao.)
2. It initiated the process of decentralisation by restoring the legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras Presidencies.
3. It also provided for the establishment of new legislative councils for: Bengal, North-Western Provinces and Punjab.
4. Recognition to the 'portfolio' system, introduced by Lord. Canning in 1859.
5. It empowered the Viceroy to issue ordinances, without the concurrence of the legislative council, during an emergency. The life of such an ordinance was 6 months.
Indian Councils Act, 1892
1. It introduced indirect elections.
2. It permitted discussions on financial matters, and allowed members to question the executive, enhancing accountability.
Indian Councils Act, 1909
Also known as Morley-Minto Reforms (Lord Morley- Secretary of State and Lord Minto - Viceroy of India)
1. Increased the size of the legislative councils, both Central and Provincial. The no. of members in the central legislative council was raised from 16 to 60.
2. Members: Official majority in central legislative council and non-official majority in Provincial legislative council.
3. It provided for the association of Indians with Executive Councils of the Viceroys and Governor (Satyendra Prasad Sinha was the 1st Indian to join, later appointed as the Law member)
4. It introduced Separate Electorate for Muslims (System of Communal Representation) i.e. Muslim members were elected by muslim voters (Lord Minto: Father of Communal Electorate)
5. Members were allowed to ask supplementary questions, move resolutions on the budget and so on.
6. It also provided for the separate representation of presidency corporations, chambers of commerce, univer- sities and zamindars.
Government of India Act, 1919
Also known as Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Montagu- Secretary of State for India and Lord Chelmsford - Viceroy of India).
1. Dyarchy introduced in provinces.
2. Classified all the subjects of administration into the central subjects and the provincial subjects.
Provincial subjects were further divided into two parts:
Transferred and Reserved Subjects.
Transferred subjects: (Governor-General not responsible)- Public health, Education, Local Self government, Agriculture, etc.
Reserved subjects: (Governor-General responsible)- Police Administration of justice, Prison, Land revenue, Finance, etc.
3. Itintroduced Bicameralism and direct elections in the country for the 1st time consisting of an Upper House (Council of State) and a Lower House (Legislative Assembly).
4. It required that the 3 of the 6 members of the Viceroy's executive council (other than the Commander-in-Chief) were to be Indian.
5. It created anew office of the High Commissioner for India in London and transferred to him some of the functions.
6. Public Service Commission was established and a Central Public Service Commission was set up in 1926 for recruiting civil servants.
7. It separated Provincial budget from central budget.
8. It extended the system of Separate Electorate for: Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.
Government of India Act, 1935 (Enforced on: 1st April 1937)
1. It abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced dyarchy at the Centre, Provided autonomy to the Provinces.
2. It provided for the establishment of an All India Fede- ration consisting of provinces and princely states as units.
3. It introduced bicameralism in 6 out of 11 provinces.
(Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam and the United Provinces).
4. It reserved certain no. of seats for Scheduled Castes, women and labours.
5. It extended adult franchise - Only 14% of total population had the right to vote.
6. Reserve Bank of India was established.
7. Federal Public Service Commission, Provincial Public Service Commission and Joint Public Service Commission were established.
8. Federal Court was setup in 1937.
9. Burma (now Myanmar) was separated from India.

10. The Act divided the powers between the Centre and units in three lists-Federal List (for Centre, with 59 items), Provincial List (for provinces, with 54 items) and the Concurrent List (for both, with 36 items)
11. Residuary powers were given to the Viceroy (Governor- General)
12. It abolished the council of 15 members.
13. Two new provinces were created: Sindh and Orissa.
14. Appointment of an Auditor-general.
15. Establishment of Federal Railway authority.
Indian Independence Act, 1947
1. It ended the British rule in India and declared India as an independent and sovereign state from August 15, 1947.
2. Partition of India and creation of two independent dominions of India and Pakistan with the right to secede from the British Commonwealth was done.
3. It abolished the office of Viceroy and provided a Governor General, who was to be appointed by the British King on the advice of the dominion cabinet.
4. It abolished the office of the Secretary of State for India and transferred his functions to the Secretary of State for Commonwealth Affairs.
5. It proclaimed the lapse of British paramountcy over the Indian princely states and treaty relations with tribal areas from August 15, 1947.
6. It granted freedom to the Indian princely states either to join the Dominion of India or Dominion of Pakistan or to remain independent.
7. The Governor-General would have full power to assent to any bill in the name of His Majesty.
8. It designated the Governor-General of India and the · vincial governors as constitutional (nominal) heads of the states.
9. It dropped the title of Emperor of India from the royal titles of the King of England.
10. It discontinued the appointment to civil services and reservation of posts by the secretary of state for India.
11. It is also known as the Partition plan/Mountbatten plan/ June 3rd plan.
At the stroke of midnight of 14-15 August, 1947, the British rule came to an end.
1st Governor General of Independent India: Mountbatten
1st and last Indian Governor General: C Rajagopalachari
